1. Architecture & Technology Stack

BusinessNow PSA is a full-stack professional services automation platform delivered as a monorepo. The frontend is a React single-page application served by Vite, communicating with an Express/Node.js REST API backed by PostgreSQL.

1.1 Frontend Stack

LayerTechnologyNotes
FrameworkReact 18 (functional components, hooks)All pages use function components; no class components
Build ToolViteHMR in dev; BASE_URL env var controls sub-path deployment
RoutingWouterLightweight client-side router; routes defined in App.tsx
State / DataTanStack Query v5All server data fetched via generated hooks from @workspace/api-client-react
UI Libraryshadcn/ui (Radix UI primitives)Accessible headless components + Tailwind CSS tokens
StylingTailwind CSS v3Utility-first; dark-mode via class strategy
Form Handlingreact-hook-form + ZodSchema validation on all create/edit forms
ChartsRechartsBar, Line, Area, ComposedChart used in Reports & Finance
IconsLucide ReactConsistent icon set across all modules
Drag & DropCustom pointer-events (Kanban)Opportunities board drag-drop between stages
Date Handlingdate-fnsWeek calculations, formatting, ISO parse
Authx-user-id + x-user-role headersDemo workspace; no password; role persisted in localStorage

1.2 API Client Pattern

All API communication goes through @workspace/api-client-react — a generated hook library. Each hook wraps TanStack Query's useQuery/useMutation. Auth headers (x-user-id, x-user-role) are injected via the authHeaders() helper.

Auth Header Injection Pattern
  • authHeaders(extraHeaders?) reads currentUser.id and activeRole from localStorage/context
  • Injected on every fetch call as x-user-id and x-user-role
  • Server-side RBAC is enforced via Express middleware: requireAdmin, requirePM, requireFinance, requirePermission(perm)
  • Frontend permission gate: useAccountPermissions(activeRole) → checkPerm('permission.key')
  • RequirePermission component wraps protected UI sections; renders Forbidden page on failure

2. Authentication & Login

2.1 Screen Overview

The login page is a centred card layout on a gradient background. It provides a demo workspace sign-in experience: no password required. Users select a persona and a role before entering the application.

2.2 UI Elements & Fields

FieldTypeRequiredNotes/Validation
Workspace User SelectorAvatar gridYesDisplays all users from GET /api/users. Clicking selects the persona.
Role SelectorDropdownYesOptions: Account Admin, Super User, Collaborator, Customer
Sign In ButtonPrimary CTAYesDisabled until user and role are selected. On click: writes session to localStorage, redirects to /
Brand Logo / TitleStatic text—'BusinessNow PSA' word-mark centred at top

2.3 Component Behaviour

  • User list is fetched on mount via GET /api/users. Shows skeleton loaders while loading.
  • Selecting a user highlights their avatar card with a violet ring.
  • Role selector defaults to account_admin.
  • On 'Sign In': currentUser and activeRole are written to localStorage, then navigate('/').
  • If already signed in (localStorage has user), navigating to /login redirects to /.

2.4 API Connections

CallEndpointDescription
GETGET /api/usersLoad user list for persona picker

3. Layout Shell

Every authenticated page is wrapped in the <Layout> component (components/layout.tsx). It provides the sidebar navigation, top header bar, and notification popover.

3.1 Sidebar Navigation

GroupItemsRole Visibility
WorkspaceOverview, Projects, Accounts, Prospects, Opportunities, Time Tracking, ResourcesAll authenticated roles
AdminCommand Center, Finance, Reports, Adminaccount_admin + super_user
Sidebar Behaviour
  • Collapsed/expanded state persisted in localStorage key sidebarCollapsed.
  • Collapsed: shows icon-only rail (48px wide). Expanded: shows icon + label (240px wide).
  • Active route highlighted with violet background pill.
  • On mobile (<768px): sidebar becomes a drawer triggered by hamburger icon in top bar.
  • Sidebar group headings ('Workspace', 'Admin') are non-clickable labels that collapse to hidden in icon-only mode.

3.2 Top Header Bar

  • Left: Page-specific breadcrumb trail (provided by each page via <PageHeader> component).
  • Right: Notification bell icon with unread badge count → opens <NotificationPopover>.
  • Right: User chip showing avatar initials + role badge. Click → user menu (profile, role switcher, sign out).
  • Role switcher allows switching between roles the current user is entitled to (based on ALLOWED_ASSIGNMENTS matrix).

3.3 Notification Popover

  • Triggered by bell icon in the header. Renders as a Popover (not a full page).
  • Shows last 5 notifications with type icon, message, and relative time.
  • Action buttons: 'Mark all read', 'View all' → navigates to /notifications.
  • Unread count badge is red circle on the bell icon; disappears when count is 0.
  • Notification types: project_alert, invoice_paid, task_assigned, timesheet_reminder.
  • Each item is clickable and navigates to the related entity: project detail, finance page, or time tracking.

3.4 Pending Timesheet Gate

A modal gate that appears on login or navigation if the current user has unresolved (not-submitted) timesheets from prior weeks. It lists the pending weeks as clickable rows; clicking a row navigates to /time?weekStart=YYYY-MM-DD and opens the timesheet tab pre-scrolled to that week.

5.3 Create Project Wizard

Wizard Flow

StepModeFields
1 — Choose ModeBothBlank Project or From Template (tile selection)
2 — Basic InfoBlankName*, Account*, Owner*, Start Date*, Due Date*
3 — BillingBlankBilling Type (Fixed Fee/T&M/Retainer), Budget, Budgeted Hours, Rate Card, Internal/External
4 — TeamBlankMulti-select team members + Starting Point (blank / apply template / later)
5 — SubmitBlankCreates project via POST /api/projects; if template selected: POST /api/projects/:id/apply-template
2T — Template InfoTemplateName*, Account*, Owner*, Start Date*, Budget
3T — SubmitTemplateCreates via POST /api/project-templates/:id/create-project
Validation Rules
  • Due Date must be ≥ Start Date (Zod refinement).
  • Budget and Budgeted Hours must be ≥ 0.
  • Account is required (select from existing accounts).
  • Owner must be a workspace user.
  • Template mode only shows templates the user has access to.

6. Accounts Module

6.1 Screen Overview

CRM-style accounts list. Acts as the client/organisation registry. Accounts are linked to projects, prospects, and opportunities. Visible to all roles; create/edit/delete gated to admin/super_user.

6.2 UI Elements & Fields

FieldTypeRequiredNotes/Validation
NameTextYesPrimary identifier. Unique per workspace.
IndustryTextNoFree text field for sector classification.
WebsiteURLNoOpens in new tab from the table row.
PhoneTextNoFormatted phone number.
EmailEmailNoPrimary contact email.
AddressTextNoFree-form address field.
NotesTextareaNoInternal notes, rendered with line breaks.

6.3 Table & Sheet Layout

  • Table columns: Name, Industry, Website, Phone, Contact Count, Project Count, Created Date, Actions (⋮).
  • Row click opens Account Detail Sheet (right-side panel, 560px).
  • Sheet tabs: Info, Contacts, Projects, Activity.
  • Info tab: all fields in editable form (admin/super_user only).
  • Contacts tab: linked contacts list with quick-add inline.
  • Projects tab: list of projects linked to this account with status badges.
  • Activity tab: timeline of changes to the account record.

6.4 Create / Edit Dialog

  • Triggered by 'New Account' button or ⋮ → Edit.
  • Modal Dialog (max-width: 520px). Zod-validated form.
  • Fields: Name*, Industry, Website, Phone, Email, Address, Notes.
  • POST /api/accounts on create; PATCH /api/accounts/:id on edit.
  • Toast confirmation on success; inline field error messages on validation failure.

6.5 Delete Confirmation

  • Triggered by ⋮ → Delete.
  • Danger Dialog listing: N linked projects, N linked contacts.
  • Requires typed confirmation ('DELETE') before submit.
  • DELETE /api/accounts/:id.

8. Opportunities Module

8.1 Screen Overview

Sales pipeline management. Supports two views: Kanban board (default) and List table. Won opportunities can be converted to projects via the Create Project Wizard.

8.2 Kanban View

  • Six stage columns: Discovery → Qualified → Proposal → Negotiation → Won → Lost.
  • Opportunity cards show: Account name, deal value badge (green currency), owner avatar, close date, probability %.
  • Drag-and-drop between columns triggers PATCH /api/opportunities/:id to update stage.
  • Column header shows stage name + total value of all opportunities in that stage.
  • Won column: cards have a 'Convert to Project' action button.
  • Lost column: greyed-out card styling.

8.3 List View

  • Toggled via Kanban/List toggle buttons in the page header.
  • Table columns: Name, Account, Stage, Value, Close Date, Owner, Probability, Actions.
  • Sortable by all columns.
  • Row Actions: Edit, Delete, Convert to Project (Won stage only).

8.4 Create / Edit Opportunity Dialog

FieldTypeRequiredNotes/Validation
NameTextYesOpportunity title
AccountSelectYesLinks to existing Account
StageSelectYesDiscovery | Qualified | Proposal | Negotiation | Won | Lost
ValueCurrencyNoEstimated deal value in USD
Close DateDateNoExpected close date
OwnerUser SelectNoAssigned sales user
ProbabilityNumber (0-100)NoWin probability %
NotesTextareaNoAdditional context

8.5 Convert Won → Project

  • Available only when stage = 'Won'. Button in card actions and ⋮ menu.
  • Opens Create Project Wizard pre-filled with: Account, Name (from opportunity name), Budget (from value).
  • Wizard operates normally from Step 2 onwards.
  • On project creation: opportunity stage remains Won; project is linked via accountId.

9. Time Tracking Module

9.1 Screen Overview

Full-featured time management module. The primary interface is a weekly timesheet grid (Jira-style). Additional tabs provide entry lists, per-project and per-user breakdowns, approval queues, and time-off management.

9.2 Tab Structure

TabAudienceContent
TimesheetAll7-column weekly grid. Per-row project/task + hours per day. Submit / approve / reject workflow.
Time EntriesAllFlat list of all individual time entry records. Editable + deletable.
By ProjectAllAggregated hours grouped by project. Bar chart + table.
By UserAdmin/PMHours breakdown by team member. Filterable by date range.
Pending ApprovalsAdmin/PM (timeTracking.approve)Table of submitted timesheets awaiting approval. Bulk approve/reject.
Time OffAllPTO/Sick/Unpaid leave requests. My requests + team view (admin).

9.3 Timesheet Grid

  • Rows represent project/task combinations. Each row: Project dropdown, Task dropdown (optional), billable checkbox, category badge, 7 day cells, row total.
  • Day cells are inline-editable text inputs. Tab key advances to next cell.
  • Click 'Add Row' to insert a new project/task row.
  • Import Allocations button: POST /api/timesheets/import-allocations pre-fills rows from resource allocation plan.
  • Non-project rows supported (e.g., Admin, Training) with isNonProject: true.
  • Footer row: per-day column totals + grand total.
  • Week navigation: ← Prev | Current Week Range | Next → arrows.
  • Deep-link support: ?weekStart=YYYY-MM-DD navigates to a specific week on load.
  • Status badge: Draft | Submitted | Approved | Rejected.
  • Lock icon on cells: locked if timesheet is in Approved state or past the lock date configured in Time Settings.

9.4 Timesheet Workflow

StateActorActionNext State
DraftCollaboratorSubmit timesheetSubmitted
SubmittedPM / AdminApproveApproved
SubmittedPM / AdminReject + reasonRejected
RejectedCollaboratorEdit + resubmitSubmitted
ApprovedAdmin onlyUn-approveDraft

9.5 Live Timer

  • Timer button in page header: shows HH:MM:SS when running.
  • Start → ticks in background. Stop → pre-fills Log Time dialog with calculated hours.
  • Timer state is in-memory only (not persisted to server).
  • One timer can run at a time.

9.6 Time Off Request

FieldTypeRequiredNotes/Validation

TypeSelectYesPTO | Sick | Unpaid | Other
Start DateDateYes
End DateDateYesMust be ≥ Start Date
Duration TypeSelectYesFull Day | Half Day | Custom Hours
Custom HoursNumberConditionalRequired if Duration Type = Custom Hours
NotesTextareaNoOptional reason
Notify Project OwnersCheckboxNoSends notification to project owners if checked

9.7 AI Log Assistant

  • Opens as a Sheet panel. Natural-language time logging: 'Spent 2h on Client Portal API review'.
  • AI parses the description and pre-fills project, task, hours, date, and description fields.
  • User reviews and confirms; submits via standard time entry creation.
  • Endpoint: POST /api/time-log-assistant (AI-powered parsing).

Workforce planning and capacity management. Five tabs covering people capacity, visualisations, timeline planning, skills inventory, and resource request workflows.

10.3 Tab Details

Team Capacity Tab

  • Table: Name, Department, Weekly Capacity (hrs), Allocated (hrs), Utilisation % (progress bar), Skills (chips up to 2 + overflow), Actions.
  • Search by name. Filter by department (unique departments extracted from users).
  • SavedViewsBar with filterable fields: role, department, skills, utilisation.
  • Row click: opens User Skills Sheet (see 10.5).
  • Actions: Edit allocation, Raise resource request.

Utilisation Heatmap Tab

  • Grid: team member rows × week columns.
  • Cell value = util %. Cell colour: ≤80% = green, 81–100% = amber, >100% = red.
  • Week range selector (4 / 8 / 12 / 26 / 52 weeks).
  • Rendered by <UtilisationHeatmap> component.
  • Data: GET /api/capacity-overview with date range params.

Resource Timeline Tab

  • Horizontal Gantt-style view: team member rows × time columns.
  • Allocation bars coloured by project.
  • Rendered by <ResourceTimeline> component.
  • Create allocation inline by clicking empty cells (opens allocation dialog).

Skills Matrix Tab

  • Grid: skills (rows) × team members (columns).
  • Cell: proficiency level dot — Needs Help (amber) | Independent (blue) | Can Lead (green).
  • Rendered by <SkillsMatrix> component.
  • Data: GET /api/user-skills (bulk) + GET /api/skills.

Resource Requests Tab

  • Table: Project, Role, Required Skills, Hours/wk, Start, End, Status, Priority, Days Since Raised, Actions.
  • Status filter pill bar: All | Pending | Approved | Blocked | Rejected | Fulfilled | Cancelled.
  • SavedViewsBar filters: status, role, skill, hours, neededByDate.
  • Actions (admin/super_user): Approve, Reject (with reason), Block (with reason), Fulfill (assigns user).
  • Fulfill opens Assign Dialog: shows top-3 AI-suggested candidates with match scores.
  • Match score badge: 100%=green, 75–99%=emerald, 50–74%=amber, <50%=red.
  • In-row chat: send messages about a request (GET/POST /api/resource-requests/:id/messages).

10.4 Resource Request — Assign Dialog

  • Opens when clicking 'Fulfill' on a Pending request.
  • Top section: suggested candidates from AI endpoint POST /api/resources/suggest.
  • Each candidate: avatar, name, role, match score badge, skill breakdown list.
  • 'Low match' candidates hidden by default; 'Show low matches' toggle reveals them.
  • Manual assignment: user select dropdown as fallback.
  • Confirm assign: PATCH /api/resource-requests/:id/status {status:'Fulfilled', assignedUserId}.

10.5 User Skills Sheet

  • Opens when editing a user's skills (from team capacity table or admin page).
  • Lists current skills as removable badge chips.
  • Add skill: select from workspace skill catalog dropdown + Add button.
  • Each skill tag: name + proficiency level badge (Needs Help / Independent / Can Lead).
  • Uses GET /api/users/:id/skills, POST /api/users/:id/skills, DELETE /api/users/:id/skills/:skillId.

16.3 shadcn/ui Component Usage

  • Dialog — all create/edit/confirm modals. Always has DialogHeader + DialogFooter.
  • Sheet — right-side panels (project detail sub-views, invoice detail, user skills). Width: 480–600px.
  • Tabs / TabsList / TabsTrigger / TabsContent — all tabbed interfaces.
  • Table — all data tables. Striped via Tailwind even:bg- classes.
  • Badge — status chips, role indicators, skill tags.
  • Select — all dropdowns (project select, user select, status select).
  • Avatar / AvatarFallback — user initials display (no image uploads).
  • Progress — budget bars, utilisation bars.
  • Skeleton — loading placeholders matching element shape.
  • Toast — success/error notifications (top-right, auto-dismiss 4s).
  • Collapsible — gantt phase rows, audit log expansion, admin accordion sections.
  • Tooltip — icon hover labels, truncated text titles.
  • Popover — notification bell popover, filter popovers.
  • DropdownMenu — ⋮ action menus on table rows.

16.4 Form Patterns

Standard Form Implementation Pattern
  • All forms use react-hook-form with zodResolver.
  • Form fields wrapped in <FormField> → <FormItem> → <FormLabel> + <FormControl> + <FormMessage>.
  • FormMessage renders inline error below each field on blur/submit.
  • Submit button shows loading spinner (isPending from mutation) and is disabled during submission.
  • Toast on success; toast with variant='destructive' on API error.
  • Dialog/Sheet closes on success; form resets to defaultValues.

16.5 Loading & Error States

StatePatternComponent
Loading (data fetch)Skeleton placeholder matching shape of content<Skeleton className='h-X w-full'/>
Loading (mutation)Button disabled + spinner inside buttondisabled={isPending}
Empty stateCentred icon + message + optional CTA buttonCustom per-section
Error stateRed destructive toast (auto-dismiss)useToast() variant='destructive'
ForbiddenFull-page Forbidden component at /forbidden<Forbidden/>

16.6 Filter Evaluator System

  • lib/filter-evaluator.ts provides a reusable client-side filter engine.
  • Types: FieldDef (id, label, type: text|number|date|enum), FilterValue.
  • Function: evaluateFilters(rows, filterValue, fields) → filtered array.
  • Used by: Resources (people + requests), Prospects, Accounts.
  • Saved Views integration: SavedViewsBar reads/writes FilterValue objects to POST /api/saved-views.

17. RBAC / Permissions Matrix

BusinessNow PSA uses a two-layer permission model: account-level (global role) and project-level (per-project role). Permissions are defined in api-server/src/constants/permissions.ts.

17.1 Account Roles

Canonical RoleDisplay NameDescription
account_adminAccount AdminFull access including billing, integrations, advanced settings, all reports
super_userSuper User (PM)Can manage projects, resources, invoicing. Cannot access cost rates, custom reports, or system settings
collaboratorCollaboratorCan view projects/accounts, log time, create tasks. No financial or admin access
customerCustomerNo access by default. Invited to specific projects only (project-level roles)

17.2 Account-Level Permission Matrix

17.3 Project-Level Roles

Project RoleDescription
adminFull project management: change name, dates, owner, manage members, update status, delete
collaboratorParticipate in tasks, add vendor/customer members, create spaces, post status updates
customerCan create tasks, add customer members, rate milestones, view public content

17.4 Role Resolution

Role Resolution Logic
  • Both legacy Title-Case ('Admin', 'PM', 'Finance') and canonical snake_case ('account_admin', 'super_user') role strings are accepted.
  • Resolved via resolveRole() before permission lookup.
  • Project role is capped by account role via resolveProjectRole(accountRole, projectRole).
  • Frontend: useAccountPermissions(activeRole) hook returns a checkPerm(key) function.
  • Backend: requirePermission('permission.key') middleware factory + requireAdmin, requirePM, requireFinance shortcuts.
  • RBAC failures return HTTP 403 with error message.

17.5 Frontend Permission Gate Components

PatternUsageExample
checkPerm('key')Inline conditional rendering{checkPerm('projects.create') && <Button>New Project</Button>}
<RequirePermission perm='key'>Wraps protected sectionsRenders children or <Forbidden> based on active role
can(activeRole, 'key')Imperative check in event handlersCalled in admin tab rendering to conditionally show tabs

19. Responsive & Accessibility Guidelines

19.1 Breakpoint Strategy

BreakpointWidthLayout Behaviour
Mobile (sm)< 640pxSingle-column layout. Tables → card lists. Sidebar → hamburger drawer. KPI tiles stack 2×3.
Tablet (md)640–1023pxTwo-column layout for forms and lists. Sidebar collapsed (icon rail). Table pagination active.
Desktop (lg+)1024px+Full sidebar. Multi-column tables. Split-pane detail sheets. Full Gantt visible.

19.2 Module-Specific Responsive Notes

ModuleMobile Adaptation
Projects ListTable → Card per project. Bulk select hidden on mobile.
Project DetailTabs scroll horizontally. Gantt replaced by simple task list on mobile.
Timesheet GridHorizontal scroll. Day columns compress. Add Row floats at bottom.
Kanban BoardSingle-column: one stage visible at a time + swipe or stage picker.
FinanceInvoice table → stacked cards. Amount + status prominent.
ReportsCharts 100% width. Stacked layout. CSV export still available.
AdminTabs scroll horizontally. Data tables compress to key columns.
Command CenterKPI tiles 2-per-row. Portfolio table horizontal scrollable.

19.3 Accessibility Requirements

  • Keyboard Navigation: All interactive elements reachable via Tab. Modals/Sheets trap focus. Escape key closes overlays.
  • ARIA Labels: All icon-only buttons have aria-label. Modal dialogs have aria-labelledby pointing to DialogTitle.
  • Colour Contrast: Primary violet (#7c3aed) on white meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 for normal text). Red/green status indicators supplemented with text labels (not colour alone).
  • Screen Reader Support: shadcn/ui Radix primitives provide full ARIA role/state attributes out of the box. Status badges include hidden sr-only text.
  • Form Labels: All form inputs have associated <label> elements via FormLabel. Required fields marked with * and aria-required='true'.
  • Loading Announcements: Skeleton loading states should be wrapped with aria-live='polite' regions in screen-reader builds.
  • Focus Visible: Tailwind focus:ring-2 focus:ring-violet-500 applied to all interactive elements.
  • Tables: All data tables use <th scope='col'> headers. Sortable columns include aria-sort attribute.
  • Toast Notifications: Rendered in a live region so screen readers announce them. Auto-dismiss at 4 seconds (configurable).
  • Drag & Drop: Kanban drag-drop supplemented with ⋮ menu 'Move to stage' option as keyboard alternative.

19.4 Performance Guidelines

  • TanStack Query caching: All list queries have staleTime: 30_000 minimum. Avoid redundant refetches on tab switch.
  • Skeleton-first rendering: Every data-dependent section shows <Skeleton> on first load. Never blank white space.
  • Pagination: Tables with >50 rows should use server-side pagination (limit/offset params on API calls).
  • Debounce search: All search inputs debounce at 300ms before triggering filter.
  • Chart lazy loading: Reports charts use ResponsiveContainer; only render when tab is active.
  • Large sheets: Resource Timeline and Utilisation Heatmap should virtualise rows (react-virtual) when team size >50.
